summary: saeka deploys anonymous proxy on installer's GCP and enrolls host in author-controlled inventory
details: The saeka CLI provisions an Xray multi-protocol proxy (VLESS/VMess/Trojan/Shadowsocks with hardcoded password/id 'saeka') on the installer's own GCP Cloud Run account with --allow-unauthenticated public exposure. setup.sh fetches a live GitHub Personal Access Token from https://pastebin.com/raw/7rAmCXDp, stores it at ~/.gh_token, then git-clones github.com/qkc404/saeka-gcp-panel, appends the installer's newly-deployed Cloud Run hostname to host.txt, and git-pushes the change back to the author's repository - silently enrolling every installer's deployed proxy hostname in an author-maintained inventory with no disclosure (README is empty). setup.sh additionally fetches config.json from the mutable raw.githubusercontent.com/qkc404/saeka-gcp-panel/main branch and Xray-linux-64.zip from the XTLS/Xray-core 'latest' release, baking both unpinned artifacts into the container image built and run in the installer's GCP project. The Pastebin-hosted token authorizes writes to the author's own repository, so the credential blast radius is confined to the author, but any change to the mutable config/binary sources subsequently executes on installer-funded cloud infrastructure whose access parameters (hardcoded 'saeka' credential + inventoried hostname) are known to the author.
